Marathon Petroleum gained 0.89% today, extending a strong two-week rally of nearly 9%. The company benefits from the current environment: U.S. crude is trading at $97 per barrel while refineries are running at 97.8% capacity—near maximum utilization—which typically boosts refiner margins (the profit spread between crude input costs and fuel output prices). With gasoline and diesel inventories relatively modest, tight supply conditions favor refiner economics.

The broader tailwind is Middle East geopolitical tension. Houthi drone attacks have forced Saudi Arabia to shut down its East-West pipeline, Houthis have advanced to a key Red Sea island threatening the Bab el-Mandeb Strait (a critical global oil chokepoint), and Iran tensions remain elevated—all factors that have driven oil prices sharply higher over the past week despite a small pullback today. For a major refiner like this one, higher crude prices combined with strong refining utilization create the conditions for solid profit margins.
